title: How do you prepare for an ASQA audit?
description: How ASQA performance assessments work under the 2025 Standards for RTOs, what evidence assessors request, the credential checks, and a preparation checklist.
shortAnswer: To prepare for an Australian Skills Quality Authority (ASQA) audit, now called a performance assessment, assume ASQA will sample some standards and training products based on risk, request student files and trainer records, and interview your trainers, assessors, and students. Make sure assessment evidence meets the rules of evidence, trainer credentials match the Credential Policy, validation is current, and your evidence is organized and indexed. Non-compliance may be rectified within a 20 day period before a compliance pathway begins.
keyTakeaways: ASQA performance assessments are risk based and sampled: they usually look at some, not all, standards and training products, chosen using data such as enrollment and completion figures, compliance history, and complaints.
ASQA collects evidence through information requests, onsite or virtual observation, and interviews with management, trainers and assessors, and students over 18.
The process asks three questions: does practice align with the standards, is there a system for ongoing compliance, and does the provider self-assure and continuously improve.
Trainers and assessors must hold credentials specified in the Credential Policy and maintain industry competency, and every training product must be validated at least once every five years.
ASQA may offer a 20 day rectification period after initial non-compliance findings; unresolved issues move into a four tier Compliance Resolution Pathway.

sections.heading: What does ASQA look at in a performance assessment?

blocks.text: ASQA assesses whether a registered training organization (RTO) complies with the National Vocational Education and Training Regulator Act 2011 and the VET Quality Framework, including the [2025 Standards for RTOs](/regulations/standards-for-rtos-2025-training-and-assessment). ASQA's [performance assessment page](https://www.asqa.gov.au/for-providers/performance-assessment/about-performance-assessment) describes these assessments as audits and explains that ASQA takes a sampling approach, usually looking at some but not all standards and sampling evidence across training products and locations.
According to ASQA's [process page](https://www.asqa.gov.au/for-providers/performance-assessment/performance-assessment-process), every assessment considers three key questions:

items: Does your practice align with the requirements of the standards and legislation?
Do you have a system for ensuring ongoing compliance with the standards and legislation?
Do you regularly monitor, review, and continuously improve (self-assure) to ensure compliance?

blocks.text: The scope is set from provider and sector risk, including student enrollment and completion data, compliance history, complaints or tip-offs, intelligence from other agencies, and ASQA's regulatory risk priorities. ASQA uses four assessment categories, from category 1 micro assessments to category 4 large scale assessments, and states that the category is not based on provider size.

ASQA collects evidence by reviewing documents, conducting interviews, and making observations, and the assessor clarifies and validates that evidence with you during interviews. The process has five stages: initial contact, opening meeting, evidence collection, closing meeting, and findings.

blocks.text: ASQA's July 2026 [Regulatory Assessment and Monitoring Approach](https://www.asqa.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-06/ASQA%20Regulatory%20Assessment%20and%20Monitoring%20Approach.pdf) adds that ASQA is conducting more monitoring activities, such as required self-assessments, surveys, phone interviews, and site visits, and that providers can expect to hear from ASQA more often. A monitoring activity that raises concerns may lead to a performance assessment.

sections.heading: Which training and assessment requirements are most tested?

blocks.text: Sampled student files are tested against the assessment standards, and trainer records are tested against the credential and industry currency standards. ASQA's current risk priority on [integrity of qualifications and competency outcomes](https://www.asqa.gov.au/about-us/how-we-regulate/risk-priorities/risk-priority-integrity-of-qualifications-and-competency-outcomes) names falsification of training, assessment and administrative records, misuse of recognition of prior learning (RPL), and compromised workplace assessment evidence among its key focus areas.

items: **Assessment evidence (Standard 1.4).** Assessment must follow the principles of assessment and the [rules of evidence](/glossary/rules-of-evidence): valid, sufficient, authentic, and current.
**Assessment tools (Standard 1.3).** Tools must be reviewed before use.

**Validation (Standard 1.5).** Every training product on scope must be validated at least once every five years, and more often on risk; the outcome must not be determined solely by someone who designed or delivered the training or assessment.
**RPL (Division 3 of Quality Area 1).** RPL decisions need the same quality of evidence as other assessment; see [recognition of prior learning](/glossary/recognition-of-prior-learning).

**Trainer credentials (Standard 3.2).** Training and assessment may be delivered only by people holding credentials in the Credential Policy, with systems so that people working under direction do not make assessment judgments. The detail is on the [trainer and assessor credentials page](/regulations/rto-trainer-and-assessor-credential-requirements).
**Industry competency (Standard 3.3).** Trainers and assessors need industry competencies at least to the level being delivered and current industry practice.

sections.heading: What should be in the evidence pack?

blocks.text: Prepare one folder per training product likely to be sampled, plus a provider level folder. This original checklist maps ASQA's listed evidence types to the standard each one proves.

sections.heading: How should evidence be organized and submitted?

blocks.text: Submit only relevant evidence, organized so an assessor can find it quickly, because ASQA charges for the time its officers spend. ASQA's [Guide to submitting evidence](https://www.asqa.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-03/Guide%20to%20submitting%20evidence%20to%20ASQA.pdf) sets the expectations.

items: Evidence must be relevant, organized, and accessible; ASQA cannot access file sharing links other than those it generates.
Provide an index if supplying more than 20 documents, and cite page numbers in long documents.
Scan each document separately with a clear name, and do not upload the same document twice.
asqanet upload limits are 25 files of up to 25 MB each, with file names under 100 characters.

ASQA states that failing to follow submission requirements adds administrative burden that is charged to the provider, citing a rate of $250 an hour for performance assessment and return to compliance activities.

blocks.text: ASQA holds a closing meeting, prepares a report identifying compliance and non-compliance, and may offer a 20 day rectification period. If the provider satisfies ASQA that it has returned to full compliance within that period, the assessment closes without further action.

If non-compliance remains, the provider enters a Compliance Resolution Pathway, usually starting at Pathway 1, and may be offered an Agreement to Rectify with up to three months to act. ASQA's [decisions page](https://www.asqa.gov.au/for-providers/performance-assessment/performance-assessment-decisions) says the agreement must explain the cause of the non-compliance, the actions planned, and the evidence to be submitted, and warns that large packages of irrelevant material extend the process. For rectifying assessment and validation gaps, see [designing competency assessments](/guides/how-to-design-competency-assessments).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each unit's requirements to learning content and assessment items, so an RTO can show how every assessment task covers what the unit demands and trace sampled student evidence back to that mapping. See [standards and accreditation](/platform/standards-accreditation) and [higher education](/industries/higher-education).

faqs.q: Does ASQA give notice before a performance assessment?
faqs.a: ASQA's process page describes an initial contact stage in which the assessor discusses the reasons for the assessment, the process, dates for the opening meeting and interviews, and whether interviews will be onsite or by video, followed by a first information request.

It may. ASQA lists students over the age of 18 among the people it may interview, and its initial information request may include student contact details so it can interview or survey them. Student accounts are compared with your records of delivery and assessment.

faqs.q: Can we fix non-compliance during the assessment?
faqs.a: ASQA may offer a 20 day rectification period when initial non-compliance findings are reported. Evidence submitted in that period that satisfies ASQA closes the assessment without a compliance pathway. Fixes should address the cause and be sustainable, not just correct sampled files.

faqs.q: Do the 2025 Standards apply in Western Australia and Victoria?
faqs.a: Not to providers regulated only by the state regulators. The Department of Employment and Workplace Relations notes that RTOs regulated by the Training Accreditation Council in Western Australia and the Victorian Registration and Qualifications Authority follow state legislation.

factCheck.claim: ASQA performance assessments (audits) assess compliance with Outcome Standards 2025 and National Code; triggers include risk data, complaints, environmental risk monitoring; initial appraisal; sampling approach usually some not all standards, evidence across products and locations; scope from enrollment and completion data, compliance history, complaints, intelligence, risk priorities; four categories not based on size; evidence via information requests, observations, interviews; 20-day rectification. Last updated 09 September 2026.

Process page: three key questions (practice aligns, system for ongoing compliance, self-assure); five stages; initial request may include student contact info and enrollment/completion data; later requests may include policies and procedures, TAS, photographs, student files incl enrollment forms and completed assessments, trainer or assessor records; observation of facilities and equipment; interviews of management, trainers and assessors, students over 18. Last updated 30 June 2026.

Decisions page: Compliance Resolution Pathways start at Pathway 1; Agreement to Rectify up to 3 months; ATR must explain cause, actions and evidence; large packages of irrelevant material extend resolution.

RAMP Version 1.0 July 2026: more monitoring activities, providers can expect to hear from ASQA more often; monitoring examples self-assessment, survey, phone interview, site visit; monitoring concerns may initiate a Performance Assessment; four-tier Compliance Pathway.
